answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, transferable bond before it may place offers, with the bond held in escrow until disputes and delivery windows close. A prism-style reputation score can weight completed trades by bond size and penalize proven fraud through slashing, while a juniper review process lets counterparties challenge claims against signed receipts. This raises the cost of multiplying identities: each new vertex needs capital tied up, and cheating risks losing it.
